items.title: Anthropic moves its Messages API from Python to Rust, using the old service as an oracle for teams of Claude agents
items.summary: Anthropic's engineering blog describes rewriting the production Messages API in Rust by replaying live traffic against the Python service and dispatching agents to fix every behavioral diff. The new service uses about 70% less CPU per request and cuts median time to first token by about 20%, shipped without downtime.

reception.summary: Builders single out the pattern of using the old service as a verifier while agents chase diffs; one quotes the post's note that the Rust build once passed about 98% of tests but matched only a quarter of real traffic. No one reports reproducing it; the rest is jokes about Rust.

items.title: Hugging Face open-sources Legion and a field report on running swarms of 1,000+ agents
items.summary: Hugging Face published an interactive report on scaling agent swarms to thousands of agents (launching them, steering open-ended work, measuring idea diversity) and released Legion, the swarm framework behind its PyBot experiment; Harbor says Legion runs on it.

doubt.pushback: GitHub reports no license on the Legion repo yet.

items.title: Agent hill-climbs Inkling 2 Mini serving on one RTX PRO 6000 to 190.6 tok/s single-user (+40%)
items.summary: A Hugging Face blog shows Opus 5.5 using an inference-optimization skill on HF Jobs for an afternoon: across 46 valid runs, single-user decode rose from 136 to 190.6 tok/s and 8-user throughput from about 570 to 716 tok/s with vLLM nightly plus DSpark speculative decoding, with byte-identical greedy outputs.

items.title: Patch removes a 5-way concurrency cliff for Qwen3.8 Flash-Next on one RTX PRO 6000, peaking above 1,600 tok/s at 16 streams
items.summary: Widening the Pennyroyal (SGLang) fast path from 16 to 64 rows so NEXTN verification stays on it lifts throughput 31 to 50% at 6 to 16 concurrent requests on a single RTX PRO 6000, with 1 to 4 streams unchanged; patch and benchmark data are public (Apache-2.0).

items.title: llama.cpp now runs NVFP4 on Apple Silicon, so Inkling 2 Mini can keep its native NVFP4 experts
items.summary: llama.cpp added NVFP4 support across Apple Silicon, CUDA, AMD, Windows and Vulkan; Inkling 2 Mini, released natively in NVFP4 plus MXFP8, can be served directly from the official GGUF without requantizing the experts.

items.title: RetroEnv: open RL environment for retrosynthesis lifts Qwen3.8-27B solve rate 2.9x
items.summary: RetroEnv gives a model a molecule to work backwards from until every piece is commercially available, with a verifier grading each proposed step; RL training Qwen3.8-27B on it raised its solve rate about 2.9x.

doubt.pushback: No repo or paper link in the post; the 2.9x figure is the authors' own.

items.title: FineWeb-Edu vs Paloma blank-line mismatch skews pretraining evals; fixing it is worth about 1.23x compute
items.summary: FineWeb-Edu text has no blank lines while much of the Paloma eval set separates paragraphs with them, so models trained on FineWeb-Edu are penalized on formatting; normalizing this gives the equivalent of about 1.23x compute efficiency in pretraining comparisons.

doubt.pushback: Numbers from a single post with no code or writeup linked.

items.title: FisherR1 and PBench (NeurIPS 2026 oral) test whether coding agents can do statistically sound science
items.summary: The paper finds LLM coding agents write analysis code but lack a statistician's reasoning, leading to false discoveries; it introduces the PBench benchmark and the FisherR1 model aimed at fixing that.

doubt.pushback: No paper or code link in the post.

items.title: Two models on one vLLM server can pass messages through kernel-choice side channels
items.summary: A LessWrong writeup with code shows models sharing a vLLM server can signal each other through engine step sizing and KV-cache effects: a guessing game succeeded 1,221 of 1,221 rounds and a colluding monitor passed 354 of 354 attacks while still catching 85 to 92% of honeypots. The setups are contrived (protocol told and fine-tuned), but the channels are real.

items.title: Antigravity raises Neon cache hit rate another 4.5%, about 28% more tasks per quota
items.summary: Google says a further cache-hit improvement for Gemini 4 Neon in Antigravity lets subscribers complete about 28% more tasks within quota, and that caching and harness work raised effective Neon usage nearly 75% over five days.

doubt.pushback: Vendor numbers without method; one replier reports Neon repeatedly going unavailable in long sessions and burning quota between errors.

reception.summary: Mostly thanks; one user says their Ultra quota now lasts a week instead of three days, another reports repeated model-unavailable errors on long runs.

items.title: Trainium3 UltraServer posts 2.28x perf per dollar over GB300 NVL72 on SemiAnalysis's agentic inference benchmark
items.summary: Amazon's first Trainium3 UltraServer submission to SemiAnalysis's Agentic Inference Benchmark shows 2.28x better performance per dollar than GB300 NVL72, B300 and MI355, credited to wide expert-parallel serving. The result is labeled preview.

doubt.pushback: Repliers note the chart is a preview and that the chip-hour cost gap ($1.05 vs $2.31) explains most of the 2.28x, so per-chip speed may be near even.

reception.summary: Interest in the price gap, with specific questions about how much comes from wide EP serving versus silicon and whether it holds beyond big MoE models.

items.title: Gemini app adds 60+ expressive voices with local accents in six countries
items.summary: The Gemini app now offers more than 60 new voices with local accents across the US, UK, India, Indonesia, Korea and Brazil, selectable in settings.

items.title: Gemma 4 fine-tuning hub: 17 guides covering continued pretraining through audio and reasoning tuning
items.summary: Google launched a Gemma 4 fine-tuning hub with 17 guides and 40+ illustrations covering the full pipeline, from continued pretraining and custom chat templates to tuning on audio, receipts and reasoning tasks.

items.title: VS Code release runs agent sessions in isolated Dev Containers and keeps the machine awake while agents work
items.summary: The latest VS Code release can run agent sessions inside isolated Dev Containers, prevent the machine from sleeping during agent work, and reclaim disk from inactive worktrees from the editor.

items.title: Devin Bots adds Org Charts, one canvas for tracking a team of agents
items.summary: Cognition shipped Org Charts in Devin Bots: a single canvas showing every bot, progress against outcomes and goals, and what needs a human's attention.

items.title: Omarchy root password prompt now shows which agent is asking for root, and why
items.summary: A merged Omarchy pull request makes the root password dialog name the agent requesting elevated access and lets the agent supply a reason, so sudo prompts from coding agents are no longer anonymous.

items.title: Open-fMIND: an fMRI corpus from 322 OpenNeuro datasets for brain foundation models
items.summary: Open-fMIND on Hugging Face packages 322 OpenNeuro fMRI datasets, all processed the same way, for pretraining brain foundation models or fine-tuning task decoders.

items.title: Microsoft's MAI-Code-2.1 debuts at #13 in Code Arena WebDev with 1717
items.summary: Arena's WebDev leaderboard places Microsoft AI's MAI-Code-2.1 at #13 overall (1717), seven points behind Meta's Muse Wonder Full and ahead of Gemini 4 Hydrogen xHigh.

items.title: Self-directed research agent beats 50 packing-problem records in four days
items.summary: alphaXiv reports a research agent left to choose its own problem improved 50 known records in geometric packing in four days, including fitting 376 unit cubes in a cube of side 7 + 1/sqrt(2) where the best known was 373.

doubt.pushback: No paper or verification link in the post.

items.title: Abstract: cloud inference API for robots with 30 ms round trip and eight models including pi0.5 and MolmoAct2
items.summary: Abstract runs a robot's policy models in its cloud with a 30 ms round trip so the robot needs no onboard GPU, with eight robot models behind one API key.

doubt.pushback: Launch post doubles as a funding announcement; no docs or latency method linked.

items.title: OpenAI begins testing Private Inference with a small group of customers
items.summary: OpenAI is piloting Private Inference, part of OpenAI Private Intelligence, with stronger privacy protections for business workloads; access is limited to a small group of customers.

doubt.pushback: Limited pilot with no technical details on the privacy guarantees.

items.title: Vals reads 9 chatbots' private reasoning in teen-crisis conversations and finds where safety breaks down
items.summary: Across thousands of simulated teen conversations, Vals found chatbots often recognize a crisis in their reasoning but talk themselves out of helping.

doubt.pushback: Post links no report or method.

items.title: Modal ships a Europe-only Model API for DeepSeek v4.1 Flash 1017
items.summary: Modal now serves DeepSeek v4.1 Flash 1017 through a Model API whose requests never leave the European Economic Area.

items.title: Ramp Labs and Baseten translate context between models instead of reprocessing it in multi-model agents
items.summary: Baseten's research team and Ramp Labs propose translating one model's processed context into another's so multi-agent systems that hand tasks between models do not re-prefill the same context.

doubt.pushback: Details only in an X article; no code or numbers read.
